news.title: Bruno Guimaraes: From Brazil's World Cup villain to the verge of Arsenal's record signing
news.lede: Just weeks after being singled out for Brazil's painful World Cup exit, Bruno Guimaraes is set to become Arsenal's record signing in a reported £80 million move from Newcastle United. The Brazil midfielder, who endured intense criticism after missing a crucial penalty in his country's last-16 defeat to Norway, is expected to sign a five-year contract until 2031, subject to a medical and official confirmation from both clubs. Guimaraes was one of Carlo Ancelotti's standout performers throughout the tournament, but his campaign became defined by one moment. With Brazil level against Norway in the round of 16, the 28-year-old saw his first-half penalty, awarded after a foul on Matheus Cunha, saved by goalkeeper Orjan Nyland.

news.title: FIFA must rebuild trust after scrapping World Cup investor proposal, says Boyce
news.lede: FILE PHOTO: The logo of FIFA is seen in front of its headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland September 26, 2017. REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann/File Photo. Aug 2 - Former FIFA vice-president Jim Boyce said on Sunday world soccer's governing body should focus on the interests of fans after President Gianni Infantino abandoned plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors, calling the proposal "ludicrous". FIFA had proposed raising up to $4.2 billion by selling a roughly 20% stake in a new entity that would oversee FIFA competitions, including the World Cup.

news.title: Football Ferns legend breaks silence on controversial call to miss 2023 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Reminder, this is a Premium article and requires a subscription to read. Former Football Ferns captain Abby Erceg, pictured during one of her last international appearances. Former Football Ferns captain Abby Erceg has no regrets over her absence from the 2023 Fifa Women’s World Cup in New Zealand and Australia, even if it was one of the toughest decisions of her career. Erceg, who will feature as a guest player for Auckland FC’s invitational team against Chelsea Women on Saturday at Eden Park, was the biggest name missing from Jitka Klimkova’s squad three years ago.

news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash

FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: Trump watches on as football explodes
news.lede: Being FIFA president carries an undeniable political dimension. “He looks like a prime minister,” people often say of Infantino when he appears at tournaments or FIFA Congresses. The power of the organisation he leads, and of the industry it represents, is immense. Infantino has dealt with major political figures in that sphere, from Vladimir Putin ahead of the 2018 World Cup to the Emir of Qatar and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for the 2022 and 2034 tournaments respectively.

news.title: Real Madrid release scathing statement on Infantino's cancelled World Cup sale
news.lede: REAL MADRID have slammed Gianni Infantino for looking to flog shares in the World Cup – and likened the bombshell proposal to LaLiga’s own commercial rights deal. Fifa were forced to scrap plans to sell stakes in the sport’s biggest tournament after facing worldwide pressure. And Infantino, 56, has vowed to keep his job despite the humiliating U-turn. But Real Madrid have hit out at the Fifa supremo for wanting to allow private investors to bag a chunk of the World Cup.

news.title: ‘They’d already moved on to Zidane’ - Didier Deschamps felt abandoned by French FA during World Cup 2026
news.lede: Didier Deschamps’ legendary tenure as France manager ended with a sense of isolation and frustration, according to new revelations regarding his final tournament. The World Cup-winning coach reportedly felt that the French Football Federation (FFF) had already mentally moved on to his successor before he had even finished his duties. The conclusion of Didier Deschamps' historic 14-year reign as France manager was marked by a sense of isolation and bitterness. Despite his unparalleled success, including the 2018 World Cup triumph, Deschamps felt the French Football Federation (FFF) had grown cold toward him during his final tournament in the United States.
